Students answer for their guests. Each student may bring one 75 cl bottle of wine, or bottled beer, lager or cider up to two pints, and no other alcohol. The [October 2023 Student Accommodation Handbook](https://www.corpus.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/downloads/corpus_handbook_06_oct.pdf) (pp. 18–19) says Upay enrolment is automatic for Corpus students and postgraduate Formal Halls are arranged with the Catering Manager. The [Catering page](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/current-students/catering) describes Formal Hall as an occasion for junior members to bring in students from other colleges and other visitors as guests. It also says Formal Hall charges are lower for College members than for guests, but gives no figure.

[Formal Hall booking](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/current-students/catering/formal-hall-booking): Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday evenings in term only, 19:30–21:00. A Downing student books themselves and up to **four guests** (five in total) through Upay. The cut-off is **11:00 two days before** the dinner, and the same cut-off applies to changes and cancellations. Arrive by 19:15 for the 19:30 seating; latecomers are not admitted and are not refunded. Each person may bring one bottle of wine, with no corkage fee. Groups of up to 20 can ask catering@dow.cam.ac.uk to be seated together by the same deadline, giving the full names of all group members; the host still waits for all guests to arrive before going in. Downing groups larger than 20 contact the Internal Events team about a private Formal Hall, non-Downing students are directed to the Conference Office rather than a private formal, and society or external university groups discuss bookings with Internal Events. No route for a non-member to book independently is published.

[Dress and conduct](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/current-students/catering/formal-hall-dress-and-conduct): gowns must be worn throughout dinner by members of the College **and their guests from other colleges**. Dress must be smart: collared shirts with a tie or cravat (collarless shirts allowed as cultural dress), smart shoes, no trainers or shorts; clean jeans are acceptable. No drinking games or drinking fines, no electronic devices once dinner begins, and photographs only after the Fellows leave. Staff may ask disruptive or drunk diners to leave, and hosts are responsible for their guests.

The [MCR Social Membership Scheme](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/postgraduate-admissions/downing-college-mcr-social-membership-scheme) is for selected postdocs and visiting postgraduate students who are **not already members of another Cambridge college**; social members may bring only one guest. It is not a route for students of other colleges.

**Practical assessment:** four weekly sittings and four guest places give a Downing host plenty of options; the host must book by 11:00 two days ahead, and guests need a gown. No measured sell-out data.

Each Emmanuel student books online for themselves; one student cannot book for another. Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday have a limit of **four non-Emmanuel guests** per person; Tuesday and Thursday are open to clubs, societies and groups, with up to **ten guests per Emmanuel student**. Book by **19:00 three days (72 hours) ahead**; group bookings need at least **ten days**. Guests must be over 18 unless the Bursar or Senior Tutor has agreed an exception. Online cancellation is free until 18:45 the day before; after that, email the Head of Catering by 10:00 on the day, after which the meal is charged. Students who started from 1 October 2025 pay through the Pay-As-You-Go system when booking.

Gowns must be worn by members of the College; the guide does not say whether guests must wear them. No toasting, singing or drinking games; photographs only after the Fellows leave or after coffee. Staff refuse admission to anyone not in a fit state, and diners must stay in their seats. Parents' Formal Halls admit close family only, with no other guests.

Booking uses the member portal, which needs a Raven login. No route for a non-member to book independently is published. An [undated Formal Hall leaflet](https://apps.emma.cam.ac.uk/college/documents/pdfs/FORMALS.pdf) gives different group nights and prices and contradicts itself on which nights take groups; rely on the 2026/27 guide. No current price is published. The guide is the undergraduate edition; postgraduate arrangements were not checked.

**Practical assessment:** six formal nights a week and a four-guest quota (ten on Tuesday and Thursday) make it straightforward with a host, but the 72-hour booking deadline, or ten days for groups, means planning ahead. No measured sell-out data.

formal.note:
The college [Food and drink page](https://www.fitz.cam.ac.uk/cafe-bar-and-buttery) says Formal Halls are open to the whole College and links the current formal menus, which list a formal **every Wednesday and every Friday** in term (18, 20, 25 and 27 November 2026, as in Michaelmas 2024 and Lent 2025); the page’s older line says “occasional Fridays”. Its booking link is labelled 'Book for Formal (Members only)'; it goes to College Bills, which needs a Raven login. Guests from other colleges therefore attend through a Fitzwilliam host.

The [2026/27 College Regulations](https://www.fitz.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-10/College%20Regulations%20for%202026-27_FINAL.pdf) (paragraph 62 and Appendix 4) say guests of Fitzwilliam members may attend, and Super Halls are normally limited to one guest per member. Entry is by University card: the host waits in the Screens for their guest and presents their card. Diners must be in Hall by 19:25; those arriving after 19:30 may be refused. Anyone who appears intoxicated is refused entry. One bottle of wine per diner may be brought in, no beer containers, and no alcohol is served from the Bar during dinner. Coining or other incitement to excessive drinking leads to ejection. Diners should generally be over 18, or over 16 with a host over 18. Dress should suit the occasion (jacket, collar and tie, cultural dress or smart evening wear) and gowns are worn; the regulations do not say whether guests are exempt.

The [2026 postgraduate welcome pack](https://www.fitz.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-08/2026%20Welcome%20Pack.pdf) asks postgraduates to book at least 48 hours ahead and says places are first come, first served. It no longer gives a maximum number of places.

Older MCR pages differ in places. The [MCR Formal Hall page](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/overview/formal-hall/), last updated October 2023, lists Wednesdays and Fridays, up to **five guests**, bookings and cancellations until 14:00 two days before, gowns for College members only (not guests), and formals by arrangement for at least 20 people. An [MCR FAQ from 2018](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/faq/formal-hall-work/) also says guests need not wear gowns. On swaps, the [MCR swaps page](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/overview/college-swaps/) says you book only yourself, with no guests, and the [MCR FAQ](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/faq/whats-the-best-way-to-attend-formals-at-other-colleges/) aims for three swaps a term and warns they sell out fast. Confirm the guest cap and deadline with the host for the current term. No current price is published.

**Practical assessment:** two formal nights a week, Wednesday and Friday, booked only by a member through a Raven-protected portal; ask the host to confirm the current guest cap and whether guests need gowns. No measured sell-out data.

KiFoMaSy itself requires a login, so the guest allowance for a given formal and the dress code are not publicly visible; ask your King's host.

The regular formal is on **Wednesday at 19:30**, fancy-dress themed, with a post-formal ent in the bar: every regular Formal Hall in [KCSU’s listings](https://web.archive.org/web/20180119143909/http://kcsu.org.uk:80/events/formal-hall-7/) falls on a Wednesday, and the [SU Alternative Prospectus](https://www.cambridgesu.co.uk/access/alternative-prospectus/colleges/kings/) describes a themed formal roughly once a week. [Varsity](https://www.varsity.co.uk/news/31242) reported in March 2026 a strict 70:30 split of King’s to non-King’s tickets, with entry checked by CamCard or QR code.

The **2025 Annual Report** says the unions renegotiated the memorandum of understanding for student-run formals, with guaranteed tickets for each union and free tickets for the students running the event. The College agreed **in principle to two student-run formals a week, funding permitting**; funding for a permanent expansion was not secured that year. An extra graduate formal was approved in Easter Term. [Annual Report 2025](https://kingscollege.shorthandstories.com/kings-college-cambridge-annual-report-2025/index.html).

**Visitors:** an outside student goes on a **guest ticket**. KCSU's 2-formals motion says "the same number of guest tickets" would be offered at the extra formals and that they would give "more opportunities for people at other colleges to attend" ([SU referendum motion](https://www.cambridgesu.co.uk/referenda/motion/59/96)); Varsity (March 2026) reports the guest-ticket limits, the 70:30 split, that members' tickets are "strictly for King's", and CamCard checks at the door ([Varsity](https://www.varsity.co.uk/news/31242)). Tickets are allocated by ballot (SU motion). The price is around £20 a ticket according to the student-written [SU Alternative Prospectus](https://www.cambridgesu.co.uk/access/alternative-prospectus/colleges/kings/).

Formal Hall is on **Tuesday and Friday in Full Term**; doors open at **19:20**. A member books themselves first and then **up to three guests** on the members-only [Meal Booking Website](https://meal.robinson.cam.ac.uk), entering each guest's full name and college; incomplete names may be refused entry. Places generally go on sale six days ahead (midnight Wednesday for Tuesday, midnight Saturday for Friday) and close at **17:00 the day before**. The undated prices are **£14.96 member / £25.83 guest including VAT**; Robinson members booked as guests pay the guest rate. A late-cancellation fee applies: the [Formal Halls page](https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/college-life/formal-halls) gives £8.87 for cancelling less than 24 hours before booking closes, while the [booking procedure](https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/college-life/formal-halls/booking-procedure) says places cancelled within 24 hours of the hall incur a fee.

**Groups:** Tuesday is the night for clubs and societies, with **up to 36 people and no member-to-guest ratio**; Friday groups are **up to 18 with three guests per Robinson member**. Bookings with more than three non-member guests must be on a Tuesday and go through the Catering Office: check availability at least 14 days ahead, then hand in the [group booking form](https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/assets/college-life/GroupBookingFormForFormalHall.pdf) with names, colleges and diets no later than one week before, when payment is taken. The organiser signs an agreement taking responsibility for guests' behaviour and for Robinson members wearing gowns. Dress is smart casual and Robinson members wear gowns. Wine can be bought at the Bar before Hall. Drinking games and excessive drinking can lead to removal or a ban.

**Practical assessment:** a Robinson member can bring three guests, and Tuesday group bookings of up to 36 make organised visits comparatively easy if arranged two weeks ahead.

formal.note:
The **2026–27 White Book** (revised August 2026) lists Formal Hall at **20:00 on Thursday and Saturday** in Full Term, Saturday only in Easter Term. The postgraduate **BA Dinner** is separate: every Friday of term at **20:00** (19:30 outside standard term), with drinks from 19:00 and no entry to Hall after 20:00 ([BA Society](https://basociety.net/ba-dinners/)). Students buy tickets on Upay. Booking opens **ten days before (08:00)** and closes **three days before (20:00)**, after which sales are final and non-refundable. Upay shows the price; the White Book gives no figure. When there is capacity, a student may bring **one guest** at a time. In exceptional cases, a student may request **one additional guest ticket** by emailing the Head of Catering **ten days before**, with a justification and all guests' full names. Hosts must accompany their guests **at all times** on College premises and enter guests' correct names. Guests must identify themselves and their host when asked. Under-18s need the Head of Catering's prior permission, and under-16s may not dine. Smart dress and gowns are worn. Photography and phones are not permitted, and students found taking part in drinking games are ejected. Some special dinners do not allow guests.

Seating follows the High Table convention: places cannot be reserved, and the White Book says groups should make other arrangements. **University societies** may not dine in Hall without extraordinary College Council permission. Trinity **college societies** may introduce guests from counterpart college societies at formal hall exchange dinners. [White Book 2026–27, §§42, 43, 45, 51, 57](https://www.trin.cam.ac.uk/download/the-white-book/?masterkey=5fe2b486e8747&wpdmdl=1228) The [Postdoctoral Society page](https://postdocsoc.trin.cam.ac.uk/formal-halls/) gives the same ten-day/three-day Upay window for postdoc bookings.

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a Trinity student to book them as their single guest on Upay three to ten days ahead and to stay with them throughout. Exchanges between college societies are the only documented group route.

The College's incoming-undergraduate page lists Formal Halls on **Thursday and Sunday evenings during term**, with Super Halls usually on Fridays once or twice a term. Dinner is at **19:30**, with drinks from 19:00. Postgraduates also have a weekly **Grad Hall** on Wednesdays at 19:30, after MCR pre-drinks at 19:00 in the Blue Room. This term's Super Halls were on Friday 30 October and Friday 20 November 2026, at 18:45 ([MCR calendar](https://mcr.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/mcr-calendar/)). Places are booked through the Meal Booking and Accounts System on the intranet. [College incoming-student page](https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/information-for-new-undergraduate-students/) The MCR links to the [meal-booking portal](https://mcr.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/useful-links/), which requires a Raven login. The College's catering FAQs and swaps-information pages are on the intranet and not public. **No public guest cap, booking deadline or price was found.**

The College dress guide applies to all students and guests: smart dress; no jeans, training shoes, beach footwear, hats or caps; jackets and gowns kept on. Members must make sure their guests comply. [College dress guide](https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/student-hub/guide-to-dress-codes/) The JCR says formals are every Thursday and Sunday in Full Term, members wear gowns, and diners may bring an **unopened bottle of wine**. Superhalls are booked through the same system; gowns are not worn, but there is a no-trainers, no-jeans rule. [JCR food and drink](https://jcr.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/college-life/facilities/food-drink) The MCR constitution makes the External Entertainments Officer responsible for **organising exchange dinners with other colleges**. formal.note:
Formal Hall is on **Tuesday and Friday in Full Term and Tuesday at other times**. Diners arrive at **19:15** for drinks and dinner starts at **19:30**. Members book and prepay through the Dining Portal. Booking and cancellation close at **12:00 noon the day before**, and some dates fill earlier. A waiting list books released places automatically, but only if the member has enough funds in their account. Members may bring **up to three non-Wolfson guests**, and all guests must be accompanied by their Wolfson host. The minimum age is 18. Places may not be sold, passed on or given away, even to another member. Diners bring the University Card the booking was made on; anyone without a University Card collects a temporary pass from the Porters' Lodge.

The dress code is formal business attire. Jeans, trainers, beach footwear, shorts, hats and caps are refused entry. Gowns are optional for members and for guests who are University members. Outside drinks, electronic devices and photographs are not allowed. The page lists **student guests at £31.56 with wine / £21.36 without**, with no academic year stated. Groups of ten or more need permission from Conference & Events at least a week ahead. A group may have at most twenty people, there is one group per Formal Hall, and each member may bring up to three guests. [Wolfson Formal Halls page](https://www.wolfson.cam.ac.uk/college-life/food/formal-halls)

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a Wolfson member to book them before noon the day before and to attend with them. When a dinner is full, the waiting list is the documented fallback.
